description:
This video introduces a new series on testing AI agents, focusing on why traditional evaluation methods fall short for autonomous systems. Discover what "agent evaluation" truly means, encompassing the entire AI stack from the LLM brain to external tools and memory. We explore a full stack checklist for system level testing and highlight the unique challenges of multi-agent evaluation, providing a real life example to illustrate these concepts.

comments.text: So unit testing (isolating the performance of individual sub-agents to which the coordinator delegates and then testing that the agents that delegate do so as expected in each scenario (and pass the relevant context)) vs e2e & Integration testing of the overall workflow - making sure assertions about the behaviour in each step assert the correct use of the outputs of prior steps, even if the prior steps outputs were incorrect, isolating the cause of failure to just the failed unit. Then performing numerous runs of the varying scenarios to account for the non-deterministic nature of agentic software - verifying number of turns (timeout) until the relevant tool was used, which tool/sub-agent was used (if the agent has multiple tools/sub-agents available to it) or just IF the tool/sub-agent was used at all (when agent is properly isolated to the extent of only having one tool/sub-agent in context), and what arguments were passed into the parameters of the tool, and if the tool call syntax itself was correct, etc.
